title: Song Literature
tagline: Early Northern Song *ci*, Su Shi, Zhou Bangyan and Li Qingzhao, Xin Qiji, Jiang Kui and the late Southern Song, Song poetry, Lu You and the Southern Song poets, Song prose, and storytellers’ scripts
summary: In the Song dynasty the song lyric (*ci*) reached its height, poetry turned towards reflection and everyday life, and the prose essay became the scholar-official’s voice. This course reads the great lyricists from Liu Yong and Su Shi to Li Qingzhao, Xin Qiji and Jiang Kui, Song poetry from the reformers of the Northern Song to Lu You, the Song masters of ancient-style prose, and the storytellers’ scripts from which vernacular fiction grew.
overview: The literature of the Song (960–1279): how ci poetry became the age's central form, how Song poetry carved a second road beside Tang, and how the marketplace of the storytellers seeded Chinese fiction.

The course runs along three co-existing supply lines—ci, shi, and prose plus vernacular narrative—so that the dynasty reads not as a decline after Tang but as a successful diversification of literary investment.

Biographies carry the map: Yan Shu's study, Liu Yong's ferry crossings, Su Shi's demotions, Li Qingzhao's flight south, Xin Qiji's unused swords, Jiang Kui's patronage—position in the empire is always also position in poetics.
outcomes: Periodise Song ci (early, Shuoshi, Huaxuan,婉约-reformists) and place key collections in it
Explain the mechanism of ci composition (qupai, tone-patterns, banquets, circulation) and its effect on style
Assess Su Shi's expansion of ci against its contemporary critics
Compare Zhou Bangyan's codification with Li Qingzhao's theory of ci's separate beauty
Characterise the Song-poetry way (liyi, lexical hardening, discourse, renyi) without the decline narrative
Compare Yang Wanli, Fan Chengda, Lu You and Liu Kezhuang as a sequence of replies to Tang prestige
Trace Song prose: guwen yiundong, essays, notes, and the political speech situation
Explain what huaben are, what they were not, and how the storyteller's craft enters fiction

chapters.title: Early Northern Song *ci*
chapters.summary: Yan Shu, Ouyang Xiu and the refined short lyric, and Liu Yong’s long lyrics for the entertainment quarters.

chapters.title: Su Shi
chapters.summary: Su Shi as poet, lyricist, essayist and calligrapher, his bold new style of *ci*, and his life in exile.

chapters.title: Zhou Bangyan and Li Qingzhao
chapters.summary: Zhou Bangyan’s craftsmanship in the long lyric, and Li Qingzhao’s lyrics before and after the flight to the south.

chapters.title: Xin Qiji and the bold style
chapters.summary: Xin Qiji, soldier and poet, patriotic lyrics, and the lyrics of Lu You and Chen Liang.

chapters.title: Jiang Kui and the late Southern Song
chapters.summary: Jiang Kui’s austere lyrics, Wu Wenying, and the lyricists at the end of the Song.

chapters.title: Song poetry
chapters.summary: How Song poetry differs from Tang: Mei Yaochen, Wang Anshi, Huang Tingjian and the Jiangxi school.

chapters.title: Lu You and the Southern Song poets
chapters.summary: Lu You’s patriotic poetry, Yang Wanli’s lively style, Fan Chengda’s poems of the countryside, and the Rivers and Lakes poets.

chapters.title: Song prose
chapters.summary: Ouyang Xiu and the reform of prose, Wang Anshi, Zeng Gong and the three Su, and Song informal notes (笔记).

chapters.title: Storytellers’ scripts
chapters.summary: Entertainment in the Song capitals, the art of storytelling, and the scripts that became the source of vernacular fiction.

history.title: A civil-service dynasty begins
history.detail: Song Taizu's settlement hands culture to the examination state: academies, printing and an official compiled anthologies.

history.title: Ouyang Xiu fixes the examinations
history.detail: As chief examiner he demotes the Taihao style; the guwen movement wins by controlling the grading key.

history.title: The Red Cliff years
history.detail: After his Huangzhou exile, Su Shi redefines what ci may hold.

history.title: The board gets set
history.detail: Zhou Bangyan systematises tune-patterns at the Bureau of Music;江西 rule-poetics forms the same decade.

history.title: The southward catastrophe
history.detail: Losing the north, the court re-founders literature at Lin'an; Li Qingzhao writes her ci essay in exile.

history.title: The poet's archive
history.detail: Lu You's ninety-four volumes;严羽's school of 'no trace' belongs to the following decades.

history.title: An unused sword retired
history.detail: Xin Qiji dies with 'Huo! Huo!' in his throat; the Han Zhou group's recovery dream is over.

history.title: Critics take over
history.detail: Yan Yu's school of Canglang answers Song poetry with Tang worship; Jiang Kui's aesthetics circulate in circles.
